title: A Voice from the Desert Comes Awful and Shrill
description: A Voice from the Desert Comes Awful and Shrill in Tonic Solfa to ST DENIO, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Drummond of Hawthornden wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 103, “"Prepare Ye the Way of the Lord!"”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens (11.11.11.11), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST DENIO; any other Elevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: A Voice from the des-ert comes aw-ful and shrill; The Lord is ad-vanc-ing; pre-pare ye the way! The word of Je-ho-vah he comes to ful-fil, And o'er the dark world pour the splen-dor of day.

lines: A Voice from the desert comes awful and shrill;
The Lord is advancing; prepare ye the way!
The word of Jehovah he comes to fulfil,
And o'er the dark world pour the splendor of day.
Bring down the proud mountain, though towering to heaven,
And be the low valley exalted on high;
The rough path and crooked be made smooth and even,
For, Zion! your King, your Redeemer, is nigh.
The beams of salvation his progress illume,
The lone, dreary wilderness sings of her God;
The rose and the myrtle there suddenly bloom,
And the olive of peace spreads its branches abroad.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Drummond of Hawthornden died in 1649.
credits: Words by William Drummond of Hawthornden (1585–1649), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST DENIO by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
